scope: Prevent native and standalone explicit-file runtimes from bypassing the managed-directory lifecycle
testFirst: The four active/closed owned-directory factory cases first failed because both factories accepted the managed database; the guard test first failed because its helper did not exist.
assertions: Native and standalone explicit-file runtime factories reject owned parent metadata before SQLite initialization, for both active and stopped managed installations
Rejection preserves database bytes and leaves the original runtime lease effective
Broken marker symlinks still identify managed storage; missing parent errors are sanitized
The console attachment and runtime factories share one marker refusal rule
limits: Trusted local operator paths remain a boundary; this does not protect against an owner replacing metadata or paths
The installed stateless Edge preview and its package are unchanged
Standalone managed-directory startup and restore activation are not implemented by this correction
